Reason: Figure 1 shows a distinct cystic lesion with an air-fluid level in the left lower lung zone, consistent with a lung abscess or infected bulla. In Figure 4, this specific cavitary lesion is no longer visible and the lung field has cleared significantly, indicating a good response to treatment (resolution of the acute infectious process). Option B is the only choice that correctly identifies the initial pathology and describes a positive clinical outcome without using incorrect terminology like "over-treatment" or claiming complete resolution of all underlying structural changes if a subtle defect remains.
